items.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: You know guys like McCoy Turner and Kenny Barron and Reggie Workman and Arthur Harper, and a lot of the Philadelphia guys like “C” Sharp, and oh, man, most of the guys around Philadelphia. And we would work tunes out.

ctx.x: It’s very important man. Because we used to have jam sessions every day of the week at different people’s houses. Okay, Sunday was my day. They had jam session at my house

on Sunday. You know guys like McCoy Turner and Kenny Barron and Reggie Workman and Arthur Harper, and a lot of the Philadelphia guys like “C” Sharp, and oh, man, most of the guys around Philadelphia. And we would work tunes out. That’s how we learned how to try to play jazz. You know we would learn the songs. You got to learn the music first. Then you learned what rhythm goes. And there are certain tunes where you can put different rhythms on you know? It doesn’t always have to be the same rhythm you know? And…

You know I wanted to ask you about taking a drum solo. You know a lot of people don’t really know how to listen to a drum solo. Many times when a drummer takes a solo on the form, the audience isn’t even counting anymore. They’re not even staying with him. Talk to us about the whole art of taking a solo on a percussion instrument.
